parole.testo: Likely borrowed from Occitan dotzena, from Old Occitan dotzena, from dotze, from Vulgar Latin *dōdeci, from Latin duodecim. Displaced earlier dodicina natively derived from dodici, which originates from the same Vulgar Latin source. Compare Sicilian dudicina.

parole.significato: to knock away the opponent's ball with one's own
parole.testo: From Occitan trucar (“hit strike”), from Vulgar Latin *trūdicāre.
